ports.note: Area is acquisition context for OSM; file inputs do not require it.

ontology.note: GeoSPARQL geometry, PROV activity and QUDT buffer units. The mode the graph was filtered for is asserted as fw:travelMode on the network entity -- the term reachability already uses for the mode it assumes -- from src/catchments.ts, so it is declared on the release whose definition is that module rather than here. Configuration SHACL is future work.

changes.description: The Inspector no longer serialises the whole network into a hidden textarea. The 'Edit bounded network JSON' control held JSON.stringify(network,null,2), rebuilt on every render inside a collapsed <details>; at the practitioner's Ituri extract (113,485 nodes, 289,080 directed edges) that was 41.8 MB built, 59.7 MB again after escaping and about 203 MB of UTF-16 per render, and Chrome killed the tab while they were simply looking at the widget. Above 20,000 nodes-plus-edges the editor is not offered and the panel says why; the file input beside it stays, so a large graph can still be replaced by a small one. Declared as the artefact cap json-editor-elements.
The travel mode says what the choice does at the control: walking keeps footways, paths and steps, driving keeps roads and their one-way rules. Shown on both the download and the extract paths.

evidence.note: Acquisition only; the graph it produces is checked where it is used. The pacing follows the service's own /api/status rather than a client-side guess, measured against OSMnx's behaviour on 2026-10-19.
